# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart valve issue, but the details are unclear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a baby, including trouble latching on and getting upset during feeds, but this seems to have resolved.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is sensitive to loud noises and covers his ears, and has possible hearing sensitivity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which causes blurry patches in his vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth that are sensitive.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia and stands and walks differently.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an unusual structure of the spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and prevent further issues
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for astigmatism and other vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor for heart valve issues and other heart conditions
* Referral for a skeletal review to monitor for hip dysplasia and other skeletal anomalies
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delay and behavioural differences
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with a tethered cord condition, which may affect him long-term, and he also experiences difficulties with finding the right words when trying to speak.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks people to repeat themselves because he didn't quite catch what they said the first time, indicating some difficulty with processing sound into understandable language quickly enough.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which means he has trouble seeing things clearly unless they're really close up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth have weak enamel, which makes them prone to cavities and sensitivity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's astigmatism and hearing difficulties may affect his ability to learn in school, especially during lessons that involve a lot of writing on the board.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulties with finding the right words when trying to speak, and may have behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with a tethered cord condition, which may affect his spinal cord and require monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers or other skeletal anomalies.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and prevent dental issues
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision and address any concerns
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor skeletal development
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and address any concerns.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond when called, and has had his hearing checked, but everything seems fine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits too close to the TV and books, and has difficulty seeing things clearly unless they're right in front of him.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent breakage

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that was found during a routine check-up and requires regular monitoring by a specialist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges during mealtimes, with eating being a struggle some days more than others, and there are difficulties finding foods that agree with her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a very small number needing longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets exhausted easily, especially during physical education classes, and has speech delays, struggling to express herself clearly when speaking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some have developmental delay, with the degree ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing, often turning the TV up loud and still asking for repetition, indicating potential hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things far away, such as the board in her classroom, and often squints or leans forward to get a better look.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist more often than her siblings did at her age, with teeth prone to cavities and requiring extra care.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, necessitating regular dental check-ups, especially with a specialist SEN dentist for those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences speech delays and has difficulties expressing herself clearly, indicating potential developmental and behavioral challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, with medication potentially being appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of spinal bones leading to increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), short fingers (brachydactyly), and curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially in the first few years, to detect and manage hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis to monitor heart conditions.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis to identify potential skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed to support developmental and behavioral challenges.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an issue with one of the heart valves, requiring regular check-ups with a cardiologist to monitor for any changes or signs that something might be off.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, with a strong aversion to certain tastes and textures, limiting her diet and making mealtime challenging. She also experiences difficulties with chewing harder foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient occasionally has episodes where she stares off into space and doesn't seem to be present, described as blank spells, which can be alarming and are being discussed with her neurologist to understand and manage better.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond right away when called, suggesting potential hearing issues, and has required grommet insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple grommet insertions and some have still required hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia (nearsightedness), for which she uses glasses to correct her vision, significantly improving her ability to see the board at school and read books comfortably.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulties with chewing harder foods due to issues with her teeth and has to adapt her diet to include softer options or cut her food into smaller pieces.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important. Regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision correction with glasses has made a big difference in her ability to see the board at school and read books comfortably, indicating a positive impact on her educational experience.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school, but the extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, leading some to transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech clarity issues, with moments where her words aren't clear or she seems to jumble them together, and there are palatal abnormalities being monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication in some circumstances. Developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe, with most children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as typical children or showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and many have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially in the first few years, to identify and manage any hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis to assess heart conditions.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis to identify any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with consideration of referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and manage challenges.
* Regular monitoring for signs of puberty and potential precocious puberty.
* Management of feeding difficulties and dietary challenges.
* Ongoing monitoring and management of neurological episodes and blank spells.
* Regular check-ups with specialists to manage and support the patient's overall health and development.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart, which was identified by doctors. The specifics and severity of this issue are not fully understood by the parents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Some may require surgery, while others only need monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, is very picky, and refuses certain textures or smells, making daily feeding a challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes where he stares off into space and doesn't respond for a few seconds, which has happened a handful of times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media last year, which was treated and cleared up. He also has issues with chewing harder foods, which may be related to his teeth or something else.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss. Many children have required multiple grommet insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear, and some have still required hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits too close to the TV and books, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with chewing harder foods like apples or meat, which may be related to his teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel. Regular dental check-ups are important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety. Medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with hip dysplasia and is waiting for the next steps in treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine. Many people have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers. A small number of children have had hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to check for vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess the structural heart issue.
* Skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for any skeletal anomalies.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address any challenges.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Regular check-ups for signs of tethered cord, especially if sacral dimple is present.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness and needs breaks during physical activity, suggesting potential cardiac issues. She gets out of breath and needs to sit down after simple play.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had significant feeding difficulties as a baby, including trouble latching on and spitting up, which have improved but still influence her eating habits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord issue, which could affect her development and movement, and she is being closely monitored and worked with therapists to help her catch up in areas she's struggling.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have neurological issues such as tethered cord, which can cause pain, weakness, and developmental delays.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, particularly in noisy environments, and doesn't always respond when called.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when looking at things, especially when trying to focus on something close up, and her eyes seem to get tired easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods and manages softer foods like fruits or cooked veggies, but struggles with tough or crunchy items.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth and may experience weak enamel, requiring regular dental check-ups and careful brushing.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delays and speech clarity issues, which impact her educational progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, and some may need to transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, speech difficulties, and moves differently compared to her peers, stumbling more frequently.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often experience developmental delays, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a slightly off gait and stumbles more frequently, suggesting potential skeletal issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review
* Dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel
* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and difficulties.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, seeming to hear some sounds but not others clearly, and may have conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had glue ear, which was treated, and now her hearing has improved.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, a condition where she sees far-away things as too close.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires more quickly than her peers during playtime or simple physical activities, which has been a concern since she was a toddler.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty consuming certain textures or types of food, leading to struggles during meals and requiring softer food options.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows signs of fatigue during mental tasks or play, and her energy levels seem to drop faster compared to other kids her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is overwhelmed by loud noises and gets frustrated in crowded or noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board in her classroom, which makes learning challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing tougher foods and requires softer options or cut food into smaller pieces.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which requires careful brushing and regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision problems affect her learning, and she may require additional support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a speech delay, which is being addressed with therapists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to check for heart conditions.
* Consider a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
* Referral for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an issue with one of her heart valves, which requires regular monitoring to prevent further complications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, which may require surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion and certain foods do not agree with her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues, making simple tasks like walking or running harder for her, and has been reported to have scoliosis.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes seems to hear clearly, but other times does not respond to certain sounds, and has required regular hearing reviews.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple grommet insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects her vision, but is being corrected.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, which can be treated with patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are prone to cavities and require constant monitoring, with regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups, especially those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) or special schooling.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues and may have developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delays.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers, and may be at risk of hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and prevent cavities.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's hearing and address any concerns.
* Ophthalmology review to monitor the patient's vision and address any concerns.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart valve issue and prevent further complications.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address the patient's coordination issues and developmental delays.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if necessary.
* Consideration of referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for any skeletal anomalies.

Parent: Our son complains that things look blurry to him. This has been an issue for a while now, and we're concerned it might affect his learning at nursery.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, he often asks us to repeat ourselves because he didn't quite catch what we said the first time. It's like he needs a little more time to process the sounds.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: The dentist mentioned his teeth have weak enamel. We're trying to take good care of them with regular brushing and dental visits to prevent further issues.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: He needs to go for regular heart check-ups due to a condition that was identified early on. The doctors keep a close eye on it to ensure everything stays under control.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He has hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone. It's something we're working with the physiotherapist to improve.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: He's very picky with food textures. Some foods he just won't eat because of how they feel in his mouth. We're trying to gradually introduce new textures to help him get used to variety.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: He has scoliosis, which we're managing with physical therapy and regular exercises to strengthen his back muscles.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart condition that requires regular check-ups to ensure everything stays under control.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky with food textures and has difficulty eating certain foods due to their texture, but there are no other reported gastrointestinal issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone, and is working with a physiotherapist to improve it. He also has scoliosis, which is being managed with physical therapy and regular exercises.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks for repetitions because he didn't quite catch what was said the first time, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision, which may affect his learning.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel on his teeth, and regular dental check-ups are necessary to prevent further issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing issues may affect his learning at nursery.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which is being managed with physical therapy and regular exercises.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage the patient's weak enamel.
* Regular hearing reviews to address the patient's hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and manage the patient's blurry vision.
* Regular heart check-ups to monitor the patient's heart condition.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and speech therapy to support the patient's development and manage his hypotonia and scoliosis.
* Consider referral for endocrine investigations if the patient's growth velocity is a concern.
* Monitor the patient's growth and development to ensure timely interventions if necessary.
